description_en: The Temple, located in the south end of the village of Lekhpur, is built with roughly cut stones and mud mortar. The lower half of the walls are plastered with ochre earth and the upper half with kaolinite. The Temple faces north-east and has pillared bays to the north-east and the south-east, as well as an opening to the north-west. A vestibule takes up nearly half of the Temple's floor space. There is a square earth (kuṇḍaoragenā) and an elevated rectangular area within it. This is the throne (gaddi,gādi) of the god's medium. The throne is in front of a door that leads to a room calledgabbir,gabhbirorgabubir, which is used for the worship of the god Lāmā.A floor plan of the Temple by Niels Gutschow was published in Günther Umbescheid's article about the story and worship of the god Lāmā (Umbescheid 1987, Pl. 2). Lāmā is an incarnated god (autine deutā). This type of divinities manifests themselves in mediums (dhāmī) during oracular consultations held at the god's temples or at the mediums' homes (Campbell 1978,Shrestha-Schipper 2003andYasuno 2018). There is no iconic representation of the god. It is thought to manifest during the oracular possessions and/or in empty niches.
monument_assessment: Good (very few light surface damages, renovated or repaired)
